description: If your child was hurt at a Georgia public school, Sovereign Immunity and official immunity stop cold most injury claims. Here is what you are up against.
shortAnswer: Sovereign Immunity protects public (but not private) schools from most lawsuits. In Georgia you can not sue a governmental employee, including school teachers, coaches, and school administrators, unless the governmental entity that employs them has waived Sovereign Immunity. Outside the motor vehicle accident injury context, the law is quite unfavorable to injured children and their families.

faq.q: Can I sue a Georgia public school if my child is hurt in a school vehicle accident?
faq.a: You generally can bring a claim if your child is injured in an automobile accident caused by a County employee. O.C.G.A. § 33-24-51 allows a waiver of sovereign immunity when a county purchases liability insurance for the negligent use or operation of a government owned motor vehicle.

faq.q: What is the difference between a ministerial and a discretionary act for Georgia school officials?
faq.a: A ministerial act is one that is commonly simple, absolute, and definite. A discretionary act calls for the exercise of personal deliberation and judgment. If an act is ministerial a school official can be held liable for negligently performing it; if discretionary, the official is immune unless the acts were undertaken with actual malice.

faq.q: Is a teacher's failure to supervise students protected by official immunity in Georgia?
faq.a: The general duty of teachers to monitor, supervise, and control students has been held by Georgia Courts to be a discretionary action which is protected by the doctrine of official immunity.

faq.q: How long do I have to send an ante-litem notice to a Georgia public school?
faq.a: Claims against public schools are subject to special ante-litem notice requirements, and the Courts are very strict in enforcing them. Generally you have only 12 months from the date of injury to properly serve an ante-litem notice on county schools and 6 months if your school is a city school.
